newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Triple P cost cuts on track, savings ahead.
newsitem.headline: Triple P cost cuts on track, savings ahead.

text.p: Triple P, the troubled Nasdaq-listed Dutch software company, said on Friday that some restructuring was on track and estimated cost savings would substantially exceed initial estimates.
"The restructurings are well on track, some are running behind and some ahead, but on the whole we're on schedule," chairman Fezi Khaleghi Yazdi said in a telephone interview.
"The cost savings as a result will be substantially higher than we expected," he later added.
Triple P said in August a 15 million guilder restructuring operation would save the firm 10-20 million guilders a year.

The Dutch maker of software applications for the healthcare, transport and banking sectors said in August it would make a loss in the third quarter because of lower than expected sales growth amid continued high sales and development costs.
Investors dumped the shares, shrugging off the announced restructurings as well as a modest share buy-back.
Triple P shares reached a low of $2 on October 9 after having reached a closing high of $14.75 in February following its flotation at $10 in December last year.
Khaleghi Yazdi said he had sold two non-core businesses in the Netherlands and expected to seal another deal soon.

"I expect the sale of the third unit today or on Monday," he said, adding that this would complete the Dutch sell-off. "We're also talking to two takeover candidates in Germany and open exclusive talks with one Belgian party soon," he said.
The seven businesses Triple P wanted to divest generate turnover of an annual 35 million guilders and will post a joint operating loss of some seven million guilders in 1996.

Triple P has completed staff cuts in Germany, axing 65 administrative and general posts. A union-backed official request for job cuts in the Netherlands was likely to be submitted to authorities next week, Khaleghi Yazdi said.

The chairman, who said that expenses for the restructuring were in line with the 15 million estimate, said he would give detailed information about the company's shape at the presentation of third quarter results at end-October.
Sources close to the company said that application sales were picking up after a slow summer, during which the company also suffered from a fire at one of its Vianen warehouses.
